title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 59-61): Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'atlas' M of 'multistructures'. It carries a refinement relation X' ≪ X and a disjointness relation X ∥ Y. That disjointness is derived from a primitive symmetric relation written with a 'between'-like symbol (≬_M). On p. 59 the hoped-for Corollary (1.58) says: if F ∥ G, F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G, then F' ∥ G'. Its proof reduced to single multistructures and then invoked an axiom At 9. Grothendieck then doubts that, in the set-theoretic ('ensembliste') case, this follows from the other axioms. Those axioms only require ≬_M to be stable under strict increasing limits and to be stronger than set-theoretic disjointness.

This page proves the independence with a counterexample. The opening lines say that this 'does not seem to imply the condition', because set-theoretic disjointness does not imply geometric disjointness.

The model:
- Take M 'reduced': each multistructure consists of a single structure. This makes the first ensembliste axiom(s) (At ens 1, 3?) vacuous.
- The three multistructures are given by sets A, B, A' with A' ⊄ A and A ∩ B = ∅.
- Put X = {A}, Y = {B}, X' = {A'}, Y' = Y.
- Then X' ≪ X, as the argument requires (the symbol is written ambiguously, see corrections). Also Y' = Y, so Y' ≪ Y.
- The set-theoretic compatibility conditions among the three multistructures already hold.
- So ≬_M can be chosen as any symmetric relation, i.e. any subset of the three pairs from {X, Y, X'}.
- Choose X ≬ Y but not X' ≬ Y. Then X ∥ Y holds and X' ∥ Y fails, although X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y.

Hence the stability of disjointness under refinement is independent of the other axioms. He therefore 'posits' (*): if X, Y, X', Y' ∈ M, X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y and X ∥ Y, then X' ∥ Y'. The parenthetical says it suffices to impose this at the level of the primitive relation ≬.

On p. 61 he declines to make (*) an explicit axiom. He sees it as a special case of a more general 'axiome de raccordement des raffinements' that does not mention 'lieux'. He then states At 9, a criterion of disjointness via components/lieux, and Atens 2: distinct points are disjoint.

The problem served is a point-free / 'tame' axiomatics of space ('analysis situs', 2nd version). Here disjointness, refinement and 'places' (lieux) are primitive notions rather than derived from points and open sets.
errors: The refinement symbol in 'X' ≪ X' is written ambiguously and could be read as 'not ≪'. For the counterexample to work, X' ≪ X must hold. Otherwise X', Y' would not satisfy the hypotheses of (*) and nothing would be refuted.

The role of the hypothesis A' ⊄ A is not explained on the page. It presumably ensures that ≪ is not just set inclusion in this model, or avoids forcing X' ≬ Y via other axioms. This is a small gap in the written argument, not an error in the conclusion.

ideas.what: Independence counterexample: a model with arbitrary symmetric 'disjointness' relation shows heredity of disjointness under refinement is not implied by the other atlas axioms
ideas.modern_name: Independence proof by small model; heredity (downward closure) of a disjointness/apartness relation

ideas.what: Axiom (*): disjointness is stable under refinement (X∥Y, X'≪X, Y'≪Y ⇒ X'∥Y'), intended as a special case of a general 'raccordement des raffinements' axiom
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity of the disjointness/non-contact relation in mereotopology/contact algebras; disjointness relations in point-free topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna, Clarke (connection calculus); de Vries and Dimov–Vakarelov (contact algebras)

ideas.what: Distinguishing set-theoretic disjointness from a stronger 'geometric' disjointness relation that is primitive in the structure
ideas.modern_name: Separation/apartness vs mere disjointness (e.g. proximity spaces, 'well-separated' regions)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics treats disjointness (via a primitive symmetric relation ≬) and refinement as primitive, with axioms like heredity under refinement. This is structurally the same programme as region-based theories of space (mereotopology, contact/proximity algebras), which the literature on Grothendieck's tame topology does not relate to.
missed.quote: on choisira X ≬_M Y, et X' non-≬_M Y — alors X ∥_F Y, mais X' non-∥_F Y, ok. On posera donc (*) ... X'≪X, Y'≪Y, et si X∥Y, alors X'∥Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would situate Grothendieck's unpublished 'analysis situs' axioms within point-free / region-based topology and allow comparison with known representation theorems for contact algebras. The page itself is routine, though.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine independence counterexample inside an unpublished axiomatics. The only interest is documentary: it shows how Grothendieck treated disjointness as primitive in his 1986 analysis-situs project, which echoes mereotopology.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Ça ne me semble pas avoir l'air d'impliquer la condition' or similar. The sense is 'this does not seem to imply the condition'.
Lines 2-4: 'disposition' is more likely 'disjonction': 'la disjonction ensembliste n'implique [pas] la disjonction géométrique'.
'la première condition A≠∅ et {3}' is likely 'la première condition At ens 1 et 3' (axiom labels), not 'A ≠ ∅'.
'X' ≪̸ X' should probably be read as X' ≪ X (the stroke is likely part of the symbol), as the argument requires.
'n'importe quelle partie de l'une des trois paires' should read 'n'importe quelle partie de l'ensemble des trois paires de multistructures X, Y, X''.
In the final parenthesis the relation is 'il suffit de poser X ≬ Y' (the primitive symmetric relation), consistent with the rest of the page.
